## Armistice acknowledgments, personnel and Warsaw radio inquiries

**Sources on this page:** p202 A1, p202 A2. [Concise case study](../radio/nov16_18_command_inquiries.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p203 A2](203.md#source-p203-a2), [p203 B](203.md#source-p203-b), [p204 B](204.md#source-p204-b), [p204 C1](204.md#source-p204-c1), [p204 D](204.md#source-p204-d).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-armistice-acknowledgments-personnel-and-warsaw-radio-inquiries"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

Seven native source records cover an armistice-receipt query, nightly radio listening, an inquiry for Captain von Borries, the location of the Warsaw general government, and radio equipment and personnel. Two previously OCR-damaged short messages become clear when their actually printed final groups are restored. All unresolved fields and missing-letter spellings remain explicit.

### p202 A1

**Source transcription — header:** `A) NKJ, UKS v LP (12.51 p.m., November 16th); FUER UKS 0900 (16), 2 TEILE; 1 TL RICHI-212`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> An OKM. Sofortige Bestaetigung erforderlich, ob Funkspruch 1XAXC?XR vom 1RX11 betr. Waffenstillstandsbedingungen

**Meaning:** Immediate confirmation is requested that a telegram on armistice conditions has arrived. The reference and date labels remain unresolved; the sentence continues in A2.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ANXOKMXXSOFORTIGEBESTAETIGUNGERFORDERLICHOBFUNKSYRUCHX1XAXC?XRXVOM1RX11MBETRXNAFFDNSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENX
```

**Edited output** — 4 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
ANXOKMXXSOFORTIGEBESTAETIGUNGERFORDERLICHOBFUNKSPRUCHX1XAXC?XRXVOM1RX11XBETRXWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The word repairs include FUNKSYRUCH to FUNKSPRUCH, M to separator X before BETR, and NAFFDN to WAFFEN. All resulting coordinate changes are priced. The opaque C?XR and 1RX11 fields are not guessed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-p202-a2"></a>

### p202 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) same two-part telegram; 2 TL RICHI-142`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> und Befehl zur Fortsetzung des Abmarsches dort angekommen. OHL 1XAXNRX1???12XOP.

**Meaning:** The continuation asks whether the order to continue the withdrawal has arrived. The OHL reference is preserved as a literal field.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
UNDBEFEHLZURFORTSETZUNGDESABMAR?CHESDORTANGEKOMMENXOHLX1XAXNRX1???12XOP
```

**Edited output** — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
UNDBEFEHLZURFORTSETZUNGDESABMARSCHESDORTANGEKOMMENXOHLX1XAXNRX1???12XOP
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source clearly prints XFGDV where the earlier OCR had X?GDV. The remaining unknowns come from unassigned cells of the published square, not missing source coordinates.
- The raw letter in ABMAR?CHES is under an unfilled square cell. The proposed S is implemented by changing its observed ciphertext coordinate, not by assigning that unknown cell S globally.

### p203 A2

**Source transcription — header:** `A) --- v ZON (23.31 p.m., November 16th); 22.35 (16/11); 2 TL RIZI-132`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> Stehet jede Nacht auf Empfang. Verbindung mit Deutschl. dringend benoetigt.

**Meaning:** Maintain reception every night; a connection with Germany is urgently needed. Only the source-labelled second part is present in this record.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
STE?ETJEDEN?CHTAUF?MPFANGXVERBINDUNGMITDEUTSCHLXRRINGENDBENOETIGTX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 2 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
STEHETJEDENACHTAUFEMPFANGXVERBINDUNGMITDEUTSCHLXDRINGENDBENOETIGTX
```

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- DEUTSCHL remains the transmitted abbreviation.

### p203 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) IWE v LP (03.48 p.m., November 18th); FUER IWE v LP 14.55 (18/11); RICHI-164`

> KM Abt. Nachrichtenmittel erbittet Nachricht ueber Verbleib Hptm. v. Borries, Gen. Kdo. ?2.

**Meaning:** The War Ministry communications-equipment section asks for information on the whereabouts of Captain von Borries. The general-command label ?2 is not numbered historically.

### p204 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) KOW v WAU (1.50 a.m., November 18th); 0115 (17), 2 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-244`

**Readable German** — based on the explicitly repaired output below.

> GE?NACH2O2. Leichte in Lomza und Czenstochau, Verbleib unbekannt. Vermutl. mit ihren Gouvs. aberueckt. Besatzg beiden anderen Stat. ohne Geraet.

**Meaning:** The whereabouts of the light units or equipment in Lomza and Czenstochau are unknown; they are presumed to have departed with their governors. The crews of the other two stations have no equipment. The opening is opaque and several transmitted abbreviations and the missing-letter spelling ABERUECKT remain visible.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LE?CHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXV?RBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITI?RENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERE?STATOHNEGERA?TX
```

**Edited output** — 2 observed-coordinate substitutions and 3 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
GE?NACH2O2LEICHTEINLOMZAUNDCZENSTOCHAUXVERBLEIBUNBEKANNTXVERMUTLMITIHRENGOUVSABERUECKTXBESATZGBEIDENANDERENSTATOHNEGERAETX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source prints four dash slots: XD--- and GG-AX. The opening GE?NACH2O2 remains unresolved.
- The source-length output ABERUECKT is not silently expanded to [abgerueckt]. VERMUTL, GOUVS, BESATZG and STAT remain their transmitted abbreviated forms.
- Part 2 advertises 282 slots but the reviewed page prints 242. A 40-slot tail-loss hypothesis yields related fragments, but is not accepted as a complete source-length decipherment or counted as another reviewed reading here.

### p204 D

**Source transcription — header:** `D) --- v --- (8.43 a.m., November 18th); RICHI-84`

**Readable German** — based on the unchanged raw output.

> Zu 2??F vom 1?X: 1. Nein. 2. PSO BSL. Fusta WAU.

**Meaning:** A short numbered reply answers no to item 1 and gives the literal call-sign-like pair PSO BSL for item 2. The inquiry number, date and expansion of PSO remain unresolved.

With the [existing shared-order assignment VA=5](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md),
the date-like field becomes **15X**. The record then fixes **40/42** positions;
the inquiry number stays `2??F`. This is a consequence of the p201/p206
order-date comparison, with no additional source edit.

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ZU2??FVOM1?XX1XNEINXX2XPSOXBSLXXFUSTAWAUXX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits.**

- The source visibly prints VAXAX and the final AXGF, both omitted from the earlier OCR candidate. The native count is 84.
- The baseline quotation keeps `1?X` before the sentence separator; the shared-order layer gives `15X`.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-nov16-18-command-inquiries-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are preserved separately. This is a source edition and explicit repair review, not a claim of universal first-decipherment priority.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For partial outputs, each certificate also constructs one injective global completion of the square and residual masks and verifies its full roundtrip; the witness is explicitly nonhistorical. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/nov16_18_command_inquiries/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A roundtrip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit"></a>

## Military-intendant addresses and responsibilities

**Sources on this page:** p202 B1, p202 B2, p202 B3, p202 B4. [Concise case study](../military/military_intendant_remit.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-military-intendant-addresses-and-responsibilities"></a>



**Source edition and recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

A four-part message distinguishes the work of the **Generalintendant in
Berlin** from that of the **Generalintendant at `GRHQU`**. It supplies a new
Berlin address on Augsburger Strasse, assigns organization, personnel and
administrative-finance questions to Berlin, and assigns supply transport,
delivery, clothing and related matters to the headquarters office. The
address number and several reference fields remain unresolved.

The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher System*,
[printed p202, PDF p205](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).
Its [preserved section image](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/sources/p202_B.png)
has this header:

<details>
<summary>Literal source transcription</summary>

**Source transcription — clear header and/or literal source record:**

```text
B) NKJ v LP (4.00 p.m., November 16th)
FUER UKS 1200 (16) 4 TEILE SS GRHQU 14/11 FLUGPOST O K M
HERMANNSTADT (16)
```

</details>

The page heading is `16th NOVEMBER, 1918.`. The published `Nov16-18` key
is used unchanged, including all eight unassigned square cells.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-b1-new-address-and-berlin-responsibilities"></a>

### B1: new address and Berlin responsibilities

The first part advertises `RICHI-228` but contains only **223 valid
coordinates**. A 228-coordinate working frame with five consecutive missing
coordinates produces a clear body. The representative below puts that gap
before received index **145**, before printed group **30**. Its raw reading
is conditional on that placement:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output — conditional five-coordinate gap before source 145; representative placement:**

```text
NEUBADRESSEX?XGENERALI?TENDANTB?RLINAUGSB?RGERSTRX??XFUERKRIEGSGL?EDERUNGENPERSONALIENFUERREINEVERWALTUNG?SACHENIW
```

</details>

Four observed-coordinate substitutions and three fills of added slots give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — same representative gap model, with the stated substitutions and added-slot fills:**

```text
NEUEADRESSEX?XGENERALINTENDANTBERLINAUGSBURGERSTRX??XFUERKRIEGSGLIEDERUNGENPERSONALIENFUERREINEVERWALTUNGSSACHENIN
```

</details>

This announces a new address and names the Berlin Generalintendant on
Augsburger Strasse. The street number and the field before the office name
are not supplied. The duties begin with war organization, personnel, and
purely administrative matters; the sentence continues in B2.

The five added coordinates are `?DGD?` in this representative. The two
question marks remain unknown. Every one of the 223 received coordinates
remains in its original order, and the four observed-coordinate changes
are recorded separately from added-coordinate fills.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-competing-placements-are-retained"></a>

#### Competing placements are retained

The [gap audit](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/gap_audit.json)
enumerates all **224** places to insert five unknown coordinates. Using an
ordinary-word template with the address and reference fields masked gives
a minimum of two observed-coordinate changes at **142 and 143**. Including
the proposed address gives three changes at **143 and 144**. Among the
**46** printed-group boundaries or final end position, the full proposed
body has its minimum of four changes at **145**; the masked comparison
instead favors **140**.

The templates were constructed after reading the candidates. These are
conditional edit-cost comparisons, not independent plaintext evidence.
The earlier book and radio language scores both favored position **146**,
and their full score rows are retained. Because marginal scores can favor
unknown characters, that ranking does not establish the original geometry.
The edition therefore uses an explicit representative and makes no unique
loss-location or loss-mechanism claim. The ordinary-language body is much
better constrained than the number fields and the precise placement.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-b2-administrative-cash-and-levy-matters"></a>

### B2: administrative, cash and levy matters

The second part contains exactly **220 slots**, agreeing with `RICHI-220`.
At received index 86 the source prints the non-coordinate letter `Q` in
`XQFDG`. A heavily overprinted final glyph in `GAAD?`, index 169, is also
left undecided. Both are masked before decryption. The raw body is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
VERPFLEGUNGSANGELEGENHEIRENFUERGELDXKASSENXGEBUEHRNISANGELE?ENHEITENFUE?KONTRIBUTIONSGELDERUNDZWANGSAUFLAGENXX
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change and two masked-slot fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
VERPFLEGUNGSANGELEGENHEITENFUERGELDXKASSENXGEBUEHRNISANGELEGENHEITENFUERKONTRIBUTIONSGELDERUNDZWANGSAUFLAGENXX
```

Together with B1, this assigns Berlin administrative victualling matters,
money and treasury business, pay or allowance matters, contribution money
and compulsory levies. No numeral is inserted into the body.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-b4-clothing-meat-sutlery-and-wartime-services"></a>

### B4: clothing, meat, sutlery and wartime services

The final part contains exactly **224 slots**, agreeing with `RICHI-224`.
Three coordinates are masked: a faded `C/G`-shaped glyph in `VDA?D`, a
faded glyph in `XAA?D`, and the printed non-coordinate `R` in `ARFXD`.
Enlarged crops preserve the visible appearances. The raw reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
BEKL?IDUNGXUXA?SRUESTUNGFLEISCHVERSORGUNG?ARKETENDEREIWESENKRIEGSLEISTUNGENXGENERALIWTENDANTXRMX?XAX????XAX11X1?
```

</details>

One observed-coordinate change and three masked-slot fills give:

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output:**

```text
BEKLEIDUNGXUXAUSRUESTUNGFLEISCHVERSORGUNGMARKETENDEREIWESENKRIEGSLEISTUNGENXGENERALINTENDANTXRMX?XAX????XAX11X1?
```

</details>

The list continues with clothing and equipment, meat provision,
*Marketendereiwesen* (sutlery), and wartime services or requisitions.
The literal `UX` abbreviation is retained. The signature says
`GENERALINTENDANT`; six positions in its reference remain unresolved.

The [shared November date and order constraints](../../experiments/nov16_18_reference_completion/README.md)
fix three of those positions, giving `RM ? A 5?5? A 11 18` and
**109/112** conditional positions. Both fives use the same observed `VA`
pair; the final eight uses `FD`. This adds no source repair and does not
complete the reference number.

<a id="edition-cases-military-military-intendant-remit-exact-costs-and-limits"></a>

### Exact costs and limits

| Part | Received slots | Working frame | Raw fixed positions | Edition fixed positions | Known-coordinate changes | Masked-slot fills | Added-slot fills |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B1 | 223 | 228, conditional | 106 / 114 | 111 / 114 | 4 | 0 | 3 |
| B2 | 220 | 220 | 108 / 110 | 110 / 110 | 1 | 2 | 0 |
| B3 | 210 | 210 | 104 / 105 | 105 / 105 | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| B4 | 224 | 224 | 103 / 112 | 106 / 112 | 1 | 3 | 0 |
| **Total** | **877** | **882** | **421 / 441** | **432 / 441** | **10** | **5** | **3** |

The [inputs](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/inputs.json) preserve
every manual row, ambiguous glyph, header and image hash. The
[certificates](../../experiments/military_intendant_remit/certificates.json)
map each plaintext position to both working-frame and original-source
coordinates, list all repairs and retain the complete unresolved domains.
There are no deletions, block moves or changes to the published square.
The two unknown inserted coordinates remain unknown.

Each partial reading has a globally consistent square/source completion
witness. Those witnesses choose arbitrary missing digits and coordinates
to demonstrate arithmetic consistency; they are explicitly **not proposed
original readings**. Repeated square cells couple the unresolved domains,
so their values cannot all be selected independently.

The period key is prior work by **George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and
Arno Wacker**, [2016, DOI 10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
B2 and B3 already appeared as unreviewed OCR-derived candidates in the
frozen p73 retrieval corpus. The present work supplies visual source
certification, the newly coherent opening and final-part bodies and their
explicit conditional models and costs. No explicit discussion of this
message was located in the bounded author-paper, supplementary-reading
and catalog check; this does not establish universal historical priority.
